turns.t: The water tablet is making me pass urine all the time, and I get cramps in my legs at night. I'm not sure it's worth it.
I understand. Let me look at your records. Which tablet is it, and what dose?
Furosemide, 40 mg, once a day, in the morning.
Doctor, I've pulled up his last blood results, the potassium was low-normal last time.
Thank you. Do you take it every day, as prescribed?
Most days. Some days I skip it if I'm going out, to avoid the toilet.
I see. Are there any other medicines?
Ramipril, 5 mg, once a day. And a baby aspirin, 75 mg.
Why were you started on the furosemide?
I have a weak heart. Heart failure, they called it.
And do you have any other conditions?
High blood pressure. And I've had my gallbladder out.
When was that?
About ten years ago.
Any chest pain, breathlessness or ankle swelling at the moment?
No. My breathing is fine, and my ankles are normal.
Doctor, I need to say that when I weighed him today, he's lost two kilos since last month.
That's useful. It could be from the water tablet, or him skipping meals. I'd like to examine him. ~
Go on.
Your legs are soft and there is no swelling, and your chest is clear.
So I'm not retaining fluid? ~
Correct. At the moment you seem to be drying out a little, which fits with the cramps.
What can we do? ~
I'd like to check your kidneys and your salts with a blood test, including potassium and magnesium.
When? ~
Today. And I'd like an ECG and a review of the dose.
Can I stop it if it's bothersome? ~
Please don't stop it yourself, with your heart condition. We'll adjust the dose after the results.
All right. I'll take it every day, then. ~
Take it in the morning, and call us if your ankles swell or you get breathless.
I will. Thank you. ~
